A Monday rule worth stealing: before you book a software demo, write down three tasks that would disappear if it worked.

Can't name three? Then it's not time to buy yet. Can name them? You've just written your brief.

What's the one task you'd most like to stop doing?
ig:
Most software buying starts in the wrong place.

It starts with a demo. It should start with a list: three tasks your team would stop doing if this worked.

If you can name them, you have a brief and a way to judge every vendor. If you can't, no demo will fix that.

What's one task you'd happily never do again?

li:
A simple rule before any software purchase: name three tasks that would stop happening if it worked.

Why it helps:
→ It turns a vague wish into a brief
→ It gives you a fair way to compare vendors
→ It gives you something to measure after launch

If you can't name three, it's usually a sign to step back and look at the process first.
